clues: This place sits in a dry valley in the west, with a tall mountain wall on one side. A huge inland sea, full of brine, spreads out on the other side.
The big sea nearby feeds extra snow into winter storms here. Snow can start in autumn and linger into late spring, piling deep in the valley.
This place did not start out as the seat of government for its land. In 1856 it took that job from a town named Fillmore.
In 1847, pioneers who had fled hard times back east founded this place by a great inland sea. They at once dug ditches to water the dry land.
The governor of Utah works in this place, and Utah lawmakers meet here. This town is where the laws of the whole state get made.
